//exports: 0.11.0 shipped pack/ - 45 files, 2.0 of this package's 2.3 MB unpacked - and
declared no subpath for it, so `exports` refused every path to it and the
published package could not do the one thing it is published for. Both keys
below are that fix, and they are for different consumers: `./pack` is the Node
loader (fs, absolute paths), `./pack/*.json` hands a bundler the file itself so
it can inline it. Node matches the exact key before the pattern, so they do not
//files: pack/ is the point of this package - the compiled JSON the engine boots from -
so it ships alongside dist/. The negations match core's: tests live beside
sources in src/, and a bare `dist` would publish compiled test modules that
import vitest, which this package does not depend on.
src/ ships because the .js.map files point into it.
